# phasetwo_realm_credential (Resource)

A service account client on a realm, for administering that realm directly — with the [Keycloak provider](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/keycloak/keycloak/latest/docs), a provisioning script, or anything else that speaks Keycloak's admin API.

Separate from the client Phase Two uses to administer the same realm. This one is yours to hold and to revoke, and a leak of it has no bearing on the other.

~> **There is deliberately no `client_secret` attribute.** Terraform writes every attribute to state, so exposing it here would put a `realm-admin` credential into `terraform.tfstate` — commonly an unencrypted file in an object store. Read the secret through the [`phasetwo_realm_credential_secret`](../ephemeral-resources/realm_credential_secret) ephemeral resource instead, which is never persisted to state or plan files.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "phasetwo_realm" "customer" {
  cluster_id = phasetwo_cluster.main.id
  name       = "production"
}

resource "phasetwo_realm_credential" "terraform" {
  realm_id    = phasetwo_realm.customer.id
  name        = "terraform"
  description = "terraform, ${terraform.workspace}"
}

# Narrow the roles where the holder does less than full administration.
resource "phasetwo_realm_credential" "audit" {
  realm_id    = phasetwo_realm.customer.id
  name        = "audit"
  description = "read-only reporting job"
  roles       = ["view-users", "view-realm", "view-events"]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `realm_id` (String) ID of the realm (deployment) this credential administers.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Note recorded on the client, to tell credentials apart later. Up to 255 characters.
- `name` (String) Short name folded into the generated client ID so the credential is recognisable in the realm's client list, e.g. `terraform` produces `api-terraform-9f3c1a2b`. Lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, up to 48 characters.
- `roles` (List of String) `realm-management` roles to grant, e.g. `["view-users", "view-realm"]`. Defaults to `["realm-admin"]`, which is full administrative access to the realm and what the Keycloak provider generally needs.

Narrow it where you can. Note that a credential without a role Terraform needs fails partway through an apply with a 403, after some resources have already been created — work the set out on a throwaway realm first.

### Read-Only

- `client_id` (String) Client ID to authenticate with, generated as `api-{name}-{random}`. Not predictable from `name`, so it is only known after apply.
- `id` (String) Same as `client_id`.
- `realm` (String) Name of the realm this credential administers.
- `server_url` (String) Base URL of the realm's Keycloak instance.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Credentials are addressed within their realm, so the id is realm_id/client_id.
terraform import phasetwo_realm_credential.terraform 3f9a1c2e-8b7d-4a11-9c3e-2f5a7b1d0e42/api-terraform-9f3c1a2b
```
